summary.text: 安 means “peaceful” or “at ease.” A roof, 宀, stands over the figure written 女. One explanation of the early forms emphasizes a person seated securely indoors: a small added stroke marks the seated posture or its support. This connects the shape with being settled and comfortable.

formation.text: The depicted building and seated figure combine to express ease. The exact motivation of the scene has more than one interpretation.

components.text: The roof represents a building or sheltered indoor setting. Some early bronze forms omit it, but it remains in the standard form.
The lower figure has the form 女, “woman.” An early-form interpretation focuses on its kneeling posture and an additional seating mark, rather than assigning a social role to the woman.

history.text: The early seating interpretation accounts for a small stroke beyond the basic roof-and-figure outline. It has been explained either as contact with the heels or as a supporting pad. Both readings connect the posture with sitting securely.

The later standard form is readily read as a woman beneath a roof. This has encouraged explanations about a woman feeling safe at home or making a home peaceful. Those are interpretations of the scene; the components alone do not choose between them.

uncertainties.text: The extra early stroke and its precise meaning remain open to interpretation. The familiar domestic stories also differ from the seating analysis. The shared idea of being at ease is clearer than one exact account of the character’s invention.

evidence.text: A woman 女 safe in a house 宀
Variously explained as (1) a woman is what makes a home feel peaceful, or (2) a woman feels safe under the shelter of a roof.
靜也。从女在宀下。

Ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意): 宀 (“house”) + 女 (“a kneeling woman”) – to be at ease, to be safe.
; calm; peaceful
: Cognate with 按 (OC *qaːns, “to push down with hand”), an exoactive derivative, literally “to cause to be settled; calmed” (ibid.).
: Starostin reconstructs Proto-Sino-Tibetan *ʔɨāɫ (“rest”), comparing it to Mizo âwl (“to rest”) (and also noting Dhimal [script needed] (el-ka, “good”)). STEDT, however, traces the Mizo word to Proto-Sino-Tibetan *s-grwal ~ *ʔwal (“finish, loose, relax”) and did not list 安 (OC *qaːn) among its comparanda: namely 完 (OC *ɦŋoːn), 緩 (OC *ɢʷaːnʔ), 諼 (OC *qʰʷan, *qʰʷanʔ), 援 (OC *ɢʷans, *ɢʷan).
